title: Shortbread
subtitle: Scottish butter biscuits
excerpt: Proper shortbread has just three ingredients and no fuss. Cold butter and a gentle oven give the classic sandy, crumbly texture.
sourceNotes: Traditional Scottish shortbread recipe using honey as the sweetener. The cold butter is key to the crumbly texture.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in a tin between layers of baking paper for up to 3 months.

content.text: Shortbread is one of the easiest bakes you can make. The secret is cold butter and not overworking the dough.
Put the flour and cold butter in a bowl. Rub together with your fingertips until the mixture looks like breadcrumbs.
Add the honey and bring the mixture together into a smooth dough. Do not overwork it.
Press the dough into a greased 20 x 20cm baking tin in an even layer.
Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 160C.
Score into 16 fingers with a sharp knife. Prick each finger twice with a fork.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until pale golden at the edges. Do not let them brown.
Cut along the score lines while still warm. Leave to cool fully in the tin before removing.

items.cause: Underbaked or butter was too warm.
items.fix: Bake for 5 more minutes and use cold butter next time.

items.symptom: Dough is crumbling and won't hold together.
items.fix: Add 1 tsp more honey and press the dough firmly.

items.symptom: Shortbread has spread in the oven.
items.fix: Chill the dough for longer before baking.
